headline.headline: BRAVES SLUG FIVE HOMERS, CRUSH PIRATES 10-5 IN PITTSBURGH
headline.deck: Olson's 25th homer headlines a five-home-run barrage as Atlanta pulls away late.
headline.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Matt Olson launched his 25th home run of the season and Atlanta added four more long balls as the Braves battered the Pirates, 10-5, Thursday night at PNC Park before 20,895 fans. Jim Karinchak earned the win as Atlanta, which trailed only briefly, put the game away with a four-run ninth inning to turn a competitive contest into a rout.

The home run parade was the story from the first pitch. Michael Yastrzemski connected for his sixth of the year, and Jarvis, Mangum and Reynolds -- Reynolds hitting his first of the season -- all went deep for a Braves offense that showed no mercy against the Pittsburgh bullpen. Atlanta took a lead in the first, fell into a tie in the third, then retook control with a three-run fourth and never looked back.

Pittsburgh managed five runs but could not solve Atlanta's pitching after the middle innings. The Pirates scored in the third, fourth and sixth but were shut out across the final three innings as Karinchak and the Braves bullpen slammed the door. The game was played in three hours and seven minutes, including a 38-minute delay.

secondary.headline: WICKENHEISER OUT AS MAPLE LEAFS PURGE FRONT OFFICE
secondary.deck: Toronto fires assistant GM Hayley Wickenheiser in a sweeping organizational overhaul.
secondary.body:
TORONTO -- The Toronto Maple Leafs sent shockwaves through the hockey world Thursday by firing assistant general manager Hayley Wickenheiser as part of a broad front-office purge, ending her tenure with the organization. Wickenheiser, one of the most decorated players in the history of women's hockey, had been a prominent member of Toronto's front office and her dismissal signals a dramatic reshaping of the franchise's leadership structure.

The firings come at a turbulent moment for the Leafs, whose playoff fortunes remain closely watched as the second round of the NHL playoffs continues. The decision to clean house in the front office mid-postseason underscores the organization's urgency to change course. Wickenheiser's departure in particular drew immediate reaction across the sport, given her stature as a Hall of Fame-caliber figure both on and off the ice.

secondary.headline: DYBANTSA DOMINATES WITH 27 IN SUMMER LEAGUE OPENER
secondary.deck: The No. 1 overall pick outshines Jazz counterpart Peterson in Las Vegas debut.
secondary.body:
LAS VEGAS -- AJ Dybantsa, selected first overall by the Washington Wizards in the 2026 NBA Draft, made an immediate statement Thursday night at the Las Vegas Summer League, pouring in 27 points to lead Washington past the Utah Jazz in a highly anticipated showdown of the draft's top picks. Dybantsa outdueled Utah's Darryn Peterson, the second overall pick, in the most-watched summer league game of the young event.

The performance lived up to the considerable hype surrounding Dybantsa, who showed the scoring versatility and playmaking instincts that made him the consensus top prospect in this draft class. Summer league results carry no playoff implications, but for a Wizards franchise eager for a new face of the franchise, Thursday night provided an encouraging opening chapter. Peterson and the Jazz will look to respond in their next outing.

secondary.headline: METS EXPLODE FOR FIVE IN FIFTH, ROLL PAST ROYALS 7-3
secondary.deck: A five-run fifth inning at Citi Field breaks open a tight game and sends Kansas City packing.
secondary.body:
NEW YORK -- The New York Mets turned a tight, back-and-forth game into a comfortable victory Thursday, erupting for five runs in the fifth inning to pull away from the Kansas City Royals and win 7-3 before 33,868 at Citi Field. Kansas City's Michael Wacha hit Mark Vientos with a pitch during the proceedings, but it was the Mets' bats that did the real damage in what became a decisive frame.

The game was tied at 2-2 heading into the fifth before New York's five-run outburst put it out of reach. The Royals, who led 1-0 after the first and matched the Mets run for run through four innings, managed only a single run in the seventh after falling behind. New York finished with seven runs on the night, completing the game in a crisp two hours and 24 minutes.

column.headline: TORONTO'S PURGE OF WICKENHEISER IS A FRANCHISE DEFINING MISTAKE
column.body:
The Toronto Maple Leafs have made plenty of questionable decisions over the years, but firing Hayley Wickenheiser -- one of the sport's most respected minds and an ambassador for hockey itself -- in a panicked front-office purge ranks among their most short-sighted moves yet. Organizations spend years trying to attract credible, accomplished front-office talent. Toronto just showed one of its finest out the door while the playoff bracket is still being decided.

What makes the timing worse is that the Leafs' problems are not new, and they will not be solved simply by shuffling the front office. The instinct to blow things up and hope for something different is understandable after years of postseason frustration, but dismissing Wickenheiser sends exactly the wrong message to every serious hockey executive who might consider joining this organization in the future. Toronto needs stable, thoughtful leadership. Thursday's purge was neither.

story.headline: RICE SLUGS TWO, YANKEES ROUT RAYS TO SPLIT SERIES
story.deck: Ben Rice drives in five as New York pounds Tampa Bay 12-4 in series finale.
story.body:
NEW YORK -- Ben Rice delivered the kind of performance that makes opposing pitchers dread the middle of a lineup. The Yankees first baseman crushed two home runs and drove in five runs Thursday night as New York blew out the Tampa Bay Rays 12-4 at Tropicana Field, splitting the four-game series before heading to Washington to open a three-game set against the Nationals.

The Yankees broke the game open with a six-run third inning that turned a 1-0 deficit into a commanding 6-2 lead. Rice's 28th home run of the season headlined the assault. Catcher Austin Wells added his fifth long ball of the year, and the Yankees tacked on three more in the sixth to push the lead to double digits. New York finished with 12 runs on the strength of timely hitting despite leaving 12 runners on base. Domingo Dominguez, Everson Pereira and others contributed stolen bases as the Yankees kept pressure on Tampa Bay's pitching staff throughout.

The Rays managed just four runs, including a 27th home run from Amed Rosario look-alike Jonny DeLuca and a solo shot from Caminero that accounted for Tampa Bay's only late resistance. The announced crowd of 18,255 at Tropicana Field watched the Yankees improve to 51-42, keeping pace in the AL East race heading into the All-Star break. Rice, now with 28 home runs on the season, has emerged as one of the more dangerous power hitters in the American League.

story.headline: DYBANTSA DELIVERS: NO. 1 PICK ERUPTS FOR 27 IN SUMMER LEAGUE DEBUT
story.deck: Washington's prized rookie outshines Jazz counterpart Darryn Peterson in Las Vegas showcase.
story.body:
LAS VEGAS — The hype was real. AJ Dybantsa, the Washington Wizards' No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, answered every question thrown at him Thursday night at the Thomas & Mack Center, pouring in a game-high 27 points to lead Washington past the Utah Jazz in one of the most anticipated summer league openers in recent memory. The teenager from BYU looked every bit the franchise cornerstone the Wizards envisioned when they locked in that top selection, attacking the basket with authority, knocking down mid-range jumpers and drawing fouls at will against a Jazz defense that had no answer.

The marquee matchup of the evening pitted Dybantsa directly against Utah's own prized rookie, Darryn Peterson, the Jazz's top selection and a consensus top-three talent coming out of the draft. Peterson showed flashes of the scoring ability that made him a lottery lock, but he could not match Dybantsa's efficiency or aggression on this night. The duel drew a packed, electric crowd that buzzed every time either young star touched the ball, a preview of what NBA fans can expect from both franchises for years to come.

For Washington, a franchise that has endured years of rebuilding, Dybantsa's debut felt like the first concrete sign that brighter days are arriving. Wizards summer league coaches raved about his composure under the bright lights, noting that he never appeared rattled despite the suffocating national attention. The full box score from the Sacramento Kings and Los Angeles Clippers summer league contest added to a packed slate in Las Vegas, but make no mistake: Thursday night belonged to Dybantsa, and the NBA world took notice.

story.headline: DUCKS MATCH $90M OFFER SHEET, KEEP CARLSSON — AND TORONTO'S FRONT OFFICE FALLS APART
story.deck: Anaheim retains its star center while the Maple Leafs gut their management team.
story.body:
The Anaheim Ducks blinked first — then thought better of it. The club announced Friday it would match the Philadelphia Flyers' record-setting five-year, $90 million offer sheet for 21-year-old center Leo Carlsson, keeping the Swedish phenom in orange at a staggering $18 million per season, the richest offer sheet in NHL history. The Flyers had submitted the aggressive bid earlier this week in a bold attempt to pry one of the league's brightest young talents out of Southern California, but Anaheim's brass ultimately decided Carlsson was too valuable to let walk.

Carlsson, who emerged as the cornerstone of the Ducks' rebuild after being selected second overall in the 2023 draft, reflected on the whirlwind with characteristic composure. 'It means a lot that the organization believes in me,' Carlsson said Friday. 'It was a strange few days, but I am happy to be staying in Anaheim.' The deal makes Carlsson one of the five highest-paid centers in the sport, placing him in financial company with Nathan MacKinnon and Connor McDavid at a age when most players are still proving themselves at the NHL level.

Meanwhile, chaos engulfed the Toronto Maple Leafs organization Friday as the club conducted a sweeping front office purge. Assistant general manager Hayley Wickenheiser, the four-time Olympic gold medalist and one of the most celebrated figures in the history of the game, was among several executives shown the door in a restructuring that signals deep organizational unrest in Canada's largest hockey market. Wickenheiser had joined the Leafs' front office in 2018 and risen steadily through the ranks, making her dismissal one of the most shocking personnel moves of the offseason.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL FREE AGENCY RESHAPES CONFERENCE LANDSCAPE
story.deck: Veteran signal-callers find new homes while draft picks settle into offseason programs nationwide.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into one of the most turbulent quarterback markets in recent memory, with multiple franchises retooling their rosters following the conclusion of Super Bowl LX in February. The Las Vegas Raiders landed veteran quarterback Russell Wilson on a restructured one-year deal worth $18 million, banking on the 37-year-old to stabilize a offense that ranked 28th in scoring last season. Meanwhile, the Carolina Panthers completed a blockbuster trade sending disgruntled signal-caller Bryce Young to the New England Patriots in exchange for two first-round picks and a veteran tight end, ending a turbulent three-year experiment in Charlotte.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held in Pittsburgh last month, continued to send shockwaves through front offices as teams assess their newest additions. Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, selected fourth overall by the New Orleans Saints, has impressed coaches during organized team activities with his pocket presence and quick release. The Cleveland Browns, selecting second overall, grabbed Georgia defensive tackle Mason Graham and have already integrated the 6-foot-3 interior rusher into their base defensive scheme, drawing praise from coordinator Jim Schwartz during early OTA sessions.

Training camp storylines are already taking shape across the league with minicamp sessions underway. The defending Super Bowl LX champion Philadelphia Eagles are navigating contract extension talks with wide receiver A.J. Brown, whose deal expires after the 2026 season. Eagles general manager Howie Roseman confirmed negotiations are ongoing but expressed confidence a resolution would come before training camp opens in late July. In Dallas, the Cowboys introduced newly signed head coach Brian Schottenheimer at a packed press conference Tuesday, with owner Jerry Jones promising the franchise would return to playoff contention after missing the postseason for the second consecutive year.
